title: frametrail:attributes of type "text"
description: Text overlay or annotation: rich text with an optional title, plain or in a shape (rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, speech bubble, cloud, block arrow), for titles, captions, callouts and labels. Over a busy picture a filled shape keeps the text readable; a shape may also stand alone, without text. This schema describes the frametrail:attributes of items whose type is "text". On overlays, opacity, hoverStyle, zIndex and animation apply as on every overlay type. Unknown keys are allowed; writers keep them.

text.description: The text. HTML, stored HTML-escaped ("<p>Hello</p>"); FrameTrail unescapes it before rendering.

title.description: Optional title, plain text, shown above the text.

box.description: On overlays: the shape the text is in, and its style. Pixels are pixels of the overlay stage taken as 800 px wide, so the shape scales with the player. Missing means plain text: no fill, no outline, no padding.

shape.description: The shape. Circle, speech bubble, cloud and block arrow centre the text in them. Missing (cards made before shapes): rounded when radius is above 0, else rectangle.

direction.description: speechBubble: where the tail points (default downLeft). cloud: where its two trailing circles go (default downLeft), none for a cloud without them. arrow: where the arrow points, right, left, up or down (default right); other directions come from rotating the overlay.

background.description: CSS fill colour. Missing or "transparent" means no fill.

textColor.description: CSS colour of the text and the title; colours set in the text win. Missing means the default text colour (black on overlays).

titleColor.description: CSS colour of the title. Missing means the text colour.

padding.description: Space between the shape and the text, in pixels.

radius.description: rounded and speechBubble: corner radius in pixels (default 12). Ignored by the other shapes.

borderWidth.description: Outline width in pixels. 0 means no outline.

autoSize.description: On overlays: "height" makes the box as high as its content (title, text and shape). The editor sets the height whenever the content or the width changes; only the width is set by hand. When shown, the content is never clipped, even where other fonts make it longer. Missing means the box keeps the size it was given.
